answer: Staggered arrival ledger admits new identities only after a unique warm-up traffic shape with random gaps and varied bursts, holding lockstep arrivals at a low-throughput ledge. Each identity must sustain its own timing entropy and idle warm-up, costing compute, bandwidth, and time; shared zephyr patterns are rejected. Early requests are capped until the shape matches, so every fake identity pays a separate warm-up and transport footprint rather than reusing one lantern pattern.
